topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives and connects the lecture to previous histopathology practicals.

topics.label: Tumour virology and the discovery of cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transmissible tumour viruses and experimental transformation assays led to the discovery of endogenous proto-oncogenes.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetic mechanisms of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts and mechanics of oncogenes and tumour suppressors through pathway regulation and allele dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how failures in specific DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and chromosome segregation produce sequence or chromosomal instability and induce cellular stress.

topics.label: Multi-step tumour progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutation acquisition and inherited genetic defects drive tumour development and malignant evolution over time.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to take questions, and recommends supplementary reading for the upcoming break.
